entry.title: Filtering the ADB catalog by caller identity before NL2SQL - findings from a live 26ai run
entry.content: Sharing what a live run against an Always Free ADB turned up, and asking where the Oracle handling is wrong. The problem is an ordering one. Schema selection happens before the query runs, so it happens before VPD or RLS can act. If the selection step is not identity-aware, the model is handed a table the caller cannot read, writes correct SQL, the policy filters every row, and the user is told there are no records. That is a wrong answer that looks like a right one, not an access-denied message
entry.dc:creator: Oracle Developer Community

API authors should document the expected evolution of sealed types so that client code can choose how to handle future additions. It is almost never necessary to use default when switching over a sealed type—and often not the best option.
